questions.enonce_markdown: **1.** You were feeling bored at home and so decided to visit your friend in the neighbouring street. A few metres to his house, you saw a young girl of about 15 sitting under a mango tree and sobbing because she has been raped by her uncle. As a counsellor, give her the necessary advice in this condition. Write in not more than 250 words.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Greet and calm the girl; present yourself as a counsellor.
2. Tell her that it is not her fault.
3. Urge medical care (within seventy-two hours) and keeping the evidence.
4. Advise telling a trusted adult and reporting to the police and the social welfare office.
5. Ensure her safety; end with hope and an offer of support.

**Model answer (230 words; the limit is 250)**

My dear child, please do not cry alone. Come and sit beside me. I am a counsellor, and I want to help you.

First, listen carefully: what happened to you is not your fault. You did nothing wrong. The only guilty person is the one who abused you, even though he is your uncle, and he must answer for his action.

Second, you need medical care at once. Rape can cause injuries, infections and pregnancy, and treatment works best within seventy-two hours. Do not wash or change your clothes before you are examined, because a doctor may need evidence. I will take you to the nearest health centre.

Third, you must tell a trusted adult, such as your mother, an aunt, a teacher or a pastor. Keeping this secret will only deepen your pain. I will go with you and speak first if you wish. The matter must also be reported to the police and to the social welfare office, so that your uncle is stopped and no other girl suffers.

Fourth, do not return to that house alone. Until the authorities act, you must stay with someone you trust.

Finally, healing takes time. You may feel fear, shame or anger; these feelings are normal, and counselling will help. You are brave, your future is still yours, and you are not alone. Now, shall we stand up and go together?

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content | 10 | The advice is complete and responsible: it is not her fault, medical care, telling a trusted adult, reporting, safety, support; no blame. |
| Style | 8 | A kind, calm, direct voice (the counsellor speaks to the girl), short paragraphs, simple words, the right register for a frightened teenager. |
| Accuracy | 2 | Correct grammar, spelling and punctuation; not more than 250 words. |

**Common errors**

- Moralising or blaming the girl, or giving only one piece of advice ("stop crying").
- Writing a story about the meeting instead of giving the advice, or exceeding 250 words.
